name: Nebius Group
thesis: STUB: Nebius Group (NBIS) is an evaluation candidate — an AI-cloud 'neocloud' (post-Yandex-divestiture entity) building out GPU data-center capacity in Europe/US, plus optionality from minority stakes (Toloka, Avride, ClickHouse) and a large net-cash position from the Yandex sale. Hyper-growth AI-infrastructure revenue against heavy capex and current GAAP losses. Thesis hinges on AI-cloud ARR ramp + disciplined capacity deployment funded largely by the existing cash pile rather than debt. Needs user-authored thesis + tier_1_kpis (AI-cloud ARR/revenue run-rate, contracted capacity, gross margin, net cash) + DCF params if/when it graduates to portfolio.
key_driver: AI-cloud ARR ramp + capacity deployment funded from net cash
thesis_breakers_qualitative: ARR ramp vs. capex pace — if contracted AI-cloud ARR stops compounding while capacity capex runs ahead, the cash pile depletes without a revenue base to show for it.
Stake monetization noise — reported results are muddied by minority-stake fair-value swings (Toloka/Avride/ClickHouse); separate core-cloud economics from holding-company mark-to-market.
Sovereign/geographic exposure — European AI-sovereignty demand is a tailwind but concentrates regulatory and customer-mix risk.

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction. (FCF/OCF and operating-loss universals deliberately omitted: a capex-heavy AI-cloud build-out is FCF-negative and GAAP-loss-making by design, so those floors would false-breach permanently — calibrate per-ticker instead.)

business_model_rules.narrative: Revenue YoY < 40% for 2Q — STUB; the AI-cloud ramp thesis requires sustained 40%+ growth as contracted capacity comes online. Sub-40% sustained signals demand or deployment is lagging the capex commitment.
Gross margin < 50% for 2Q — STUB calibration floor; sustained sub-50% GM would indicate under-utilized capacity or pricing pressure undermining the path to operating leverage.
